meta.title: Wedding Ceremony — Complete Guide | Mariable
meta.description: Complete guide for your wedding ceremony: secular ceremony, Catholic wedding, rituals, vows, music and logistics.

common.premiumLaiqueDescription: Download the complete checklist for your secular ceremony.
common.premiumCatholiqueDescription: Download the complete checklist for your Catholic wedding.

laique.fondamentauxIntro: The secular ceremony is the emotional centerpiece of the wedding — a space of total freedom where your story becomes the heart of the narrative.

fondamentaux.label: Possible venues
fondamentaux.value: Gardens, estates, beaches, museums, unusual venues

deroulementEtapes.description: Bride and groom on a parent's arm, witnesses, flower children
The officiant sets the tone; tribute to absent loved ones possible
Story of how they met, hardships overcome, plans for the future
Sand, ribbons, tree... a tangible gesture to sacralize the union
The couple speaks directly to each other — the most moving moment
Explicit consent guided by the officiant
Cheers, flower petals or soap bubbles

vigilances: Higher mental load on the day

rituels.description: Mix two sands of different colors into a single vase. The grains blend irreversibly, symbolizing the union of two personalities.
rituels.conseils: Pick contrasting colors. Keep the vase as a keepsake.

rituels.description: Of Celtic origin, this ritual binds the couple's hands with ribbons of different colors. Each ribbon can be brought by a loved one.
rituels.conseils: Ribbons of at least 1.2 m long and 4 cm wide for a striking visual effect.

rituels.description: The couple plants a sapling together, symbolizing the growth of their love and the need to nurture it daily.
rituels.conseils: Pick a tree suited to your garden. Roots = foundations, branches = shared future.

rituels.description: Each guest holds a stone and symbolically places a wish for the couple on it. The stones are collected in a jar.
rituels.conseils: Great for involving a large audience silently and solemnly.

rituels.description: A ball of yarn is tossed among the guests, creating a physical web that ties everyone to the couple.
rituels.conseils: Not recommended if guests have elaborate hairdos or large hats!

rolesProches.description: Share an anecdote, a poem or a literary text
A trusted role, often given to children or witnesses
Lighting a candle, tying a ribbon, pouring sand
Solemn moment at the end of the ceremony

alternativesTimides: Speaking as a duo (two people for mutual support)
Silent roles (carrying the rings, handing out programs)
A photo or video montage to project
Reading texts from famous authors (less intimidating than writing your own)
voeuxPreparationItems: Start jotting down ideas 2–3 months ahead in a small notebook
Collect memories, daily proofs of love, inspiring quotes
Finalize the version 15 days before to stay connected to the emotion

voeuxStructureItems.title: 1. The past
voeuxStructureItems.desc: Recall a striking memory or your first meeting

voeuxStructureItems.title: 2. The present
voeuxStructureItems.desc: What your partner means today (refuge, strength, certainty)

voeuxStructureItems.title: 3. The future
voeuxStructureItems.desc: Concrete promises, big plans and small everyday details

voeuxStructureItems.title: 4. The conclusion
voeuxStructureItems.desc: A simple sentence sealing the commitment

voeuxConseilsItems: Length: 2 to 3 minutes to captivate without dragging
Authenticity: if you're funny, add humor. If you're reserved, simplicity is enough
Format: avoid the phone! Use beautiful paper for the photos
Emotion: don't be afraid to cry or pause
planBItems: Plan a backup venue (hall, barn, marquee)
In case of heat wave: shade and refreshments
sonoItems: At least 2 wireless mics for 50+ guests
Speakers near the guests (not behind the couple)
Check power outlets or rent a silent generator
amenagementItems: Cover plastic chairs (they get hot in the sun)
Couple at a 3/4 angle to the audience
laique.musiqueNote: A live band can adapt in real time. If using a DJ: share the precise cue sheet.

retroplanning.action: Finalize the script with the officiant, send music to the DJ, confirm speakers
Read your vows aloud, prepare an emergency kit (tissues, water, makeup)
On-site rehearsal, set up decor, check the mics
Take 5 minutes together before the start to recenter

laique.citation: "The secular ceremony, far more than a simple alternative to a religious setting, is a true engineering of emotion. By placing the couple's story at the center, it turns guests from spectators into active witnesses of the commitment."

catholique.introQuote: The Catholic wedding is a sacramental act where the divine meets the human to seal an indissoluble covenant.
catholique.alertText: The civil wedding must take place before the religious one. Preparation should ideally start 1 year ahead, or at least 6 months before.
catholique.mixtesTitle: Mixed weddings and disparity of cult
catholique.mixteCardText: Union between two baptized persons (e.g. Catholic and Protestant).
catholique.mixteCardNote: Requires the bishop's authorization, requested by the priest.
catholique.disparityCardText: Union between a Catholic and an unbaptized person.
catholique.disparityCardNote: Requires a dispensation. The Catholic spouse commits to the children's baptism.
catholique.piliersNote: Each spouse writes a handwritten declaration of intent expressing their adherence to these 4 pillars.

piliersMariage.pratique: Mature commitment, free from family or social pressure
Promise of mutual support in sickness and in health
Willingness to build a lasting home, until death do us part
Desire to welcome children or generous openness to others

catholique.prepPretreText: 3 to 4 meetings to explore the couple's spiritual dimension, their understanding of the sacrament, and the writing of the declarations of intent.
catholique.prepCpmText: Day or weekend sessions with other engaged couples to address communication, conflict management, sexuality, and life plans.

derouleCatholique.description: The groom enters on his mother's arm, followed by the procession, then the bride on her father's arm
Biblical readings (Old Testament, Epistles, Gospel) and the priest's homily
The priest asks the couple about their freedom and commitment
The couple bestows the sacrament on each other
The rings are blessed and exchanged as a sign of the covenant
Solemn prayer invoking the strength of the Holy Spirit on the couple
Accompanied by music, followed by the offering
The couple leaves the church amid cheers

catholique.decoNote: Plan a team to remove the decorations after the ceremony.
catholique.decoAutelText: Focal point of the liturgy. Floral compositions at the base or on the sides, never directly on the altar.
catholique.decoAlleeText: Pew-end bouquets, silk or satin ribbons, flower petals if the parish allows.
catholique.decoBougiesText: They symbolize the light of Christ. Possible ritual: together lighting a central candle from two side candles.
catholique.musiqueNote: The organ remains the instrument of choice. A gospel choir or string quartet are possible for a personal touch.

musiqueSacree.exemples: Psalm 127, Alleluia from Taizé or Handel
Ave Maria (Schubert or Gounod), Panis Angelicus
Cantique de Jean Racine, Anima Christi

rolesTemoinsItems: At least 2 witnesses (1 per spouse), not necessarily baptized
They sign the register to certify the exchange of consents
rolesEnfantsItems: Carry the rings on a cushion
Toss flower petals before the bride
Hold the train of the dress if needed
Ideal age: 5 to 10 years old to minimize surprises
rolesPhotosItems: Introduce themselves to the priest before the ceremony
Stay outside the choir, with slow and discreet movements
Favor telephoto lenses to keep their distance
Key moments: entry, rings, blessing, signing
catholique.sortieNote: Check with the parish what is allowed. Plan for cleaning the forecourt.

items: Confirm the date with the parish

catholique.citation: "The Catholic wedding is a delicate balance between liturgical rigor and the expression of personal love. The celebration is not an end in itself, but the beginning of a covenant sustained by faith and community."

notes: Preparation should start 6 to 12 months before the wedding
The civil wedding must precede the religious one
Plan 3 to 4 meetings with the priest and CPM sessions
The ceremony lasts approximately 1h to 1h30 (nuptial Mass)
